intro: Raid Scout searches Twitch in a creator-controlled order, filters unsafe or repetitive destinations, and suggests one live channel. Use Finish Stream for one creator-controlled end-to-end run, or Suggest then Confirm when you want to review the destination first.

labels.suggest-only: Suggest only; never start a raid

sections.title: 1. Turn on Raid Scout
sections.description: Start here. Finish Stream runs the complete configured ending flow with one creator press. Suggest and Confirm keep destination review separate, and the exact ending scene can start one search per live stream.

sections.title: 2. Where to search
sections.description: Raid Scout checks your preferred/local list first and picks its lowest-viewer live channel. If none qualify, it checks followed-live channels and picks the lowest; only then does it check the current category and pick the lowest there.

sections.title: 3. Preferred channels and viewer suggestions
sections.description: Your permanent list stays saved. Twitch and Kick use native rewards; YouTube and TikTok use Viewer Foundation points with the configured command. Suggestions clear after the stream.
sections.notice: Recommended Twitch/Kick reward — title: Raid Scout Suggestion; cost: 500; color: #F59E0B; description: 'Suggest one Twitch channel for tonight raid search.' Viewer input required. Keep Skip Reward Queue disabled on Twitch so the controller can fulfill/refund it. Kick cannot currently be fulfilled or refunded by Streamer.bot, so a rejected Kick suggestion still spends the reward. YouTube and TikTok point spends are rolled back if saving fails.

sections.title: 4. Search limits
sections.description: Only limits for enabled search sources are shown. Conservative limits keep Twitch requests fast and bounded.

sections.title: 5. Audience size
sections.description: Set the allowed viewer range. Within each tier, Raid Scout selects the eligible live channel with the fewest viewers; the bounded fallback prevents a popular category from leaving the ending flow without a destination.

sections.title: 6. Language, category, and tags
sections.description: Require a matching language when needed, then exclude categories or tags you do not want recommended.

sections.title: 7. Blocked channels and repeat protection
sections.description: Your own channel, offline channels, the current suggestion, blocked channels, and recent confirmed raids are always removed.

sections.title: Legacy selection settings
sections.description: These saved values are preserved for upgrade compatibility but no longer affect selection. Raid Scout chooses the fewest viewers inside the first available preferred, followed, or category tier.

sections.title: 8. Confirmation and chat messages
sections.description: Set how long a suggestion remains valid and choose which outcomes should be announced in chat. Message boxes appear only when their announcement is enabled.

sections.title: 9. Search progress and cards
sections.description: Use the add-on URL privately as a dock to watch Raid Scout check each source. Search steps stay out of chat; disable suggestion cards only when an unconfirmed destination must remain private from the on-stream source.

sections.title: 10. Optional raid clip preview
sections.description: After you Confirm a suggestion, optionally play one public clip from that channel all the way through before Twitch starts the raid. The ending ad already runs in parallel from Suggest, giving discovery and playback useful time without cutting the clip short.
sections.notice: The recommended pause option uses StreamBridge's single internal video slot: Random Clip Player fades out without being disabled, Raid Scout buffers and plays its selected clip, and cancellation or failure allows normal playback to resume. Playback starts only after the browser source reports enough media buffered to continue.

sections.title: 11. Optional automatic broadcast ending
sections.description: Suggest or Finish Stream immediately starts or adopts the ending Twitch ad. Discovery, review, and full clip playback continue during the commercial; after the raid attempt, every broadcast stops when the genuine ad timer finishes even if Twitch rejects or cannot confirm the raid.
sections.notice: Recommended: choose After the Twitch ad finishes. Raid Scout never requests a second ad for the same ending flow. A rejected raid no longer blocks shutdown, but a missing genuine Ad Run signal still leaves every broadcast live because there is no trustworthy timer. OBS/Aitum uses the included Stop All OBS Streaming Outputs action, which targets Aitum's stable output names plus RTMP, WHIP, FTL, and MPEG-TS service outputs before stopping OBS main. Recording, replay buffer, and virtual camera are excluded. Attach Twitch > Ads > Ad Run to Ad Break Companion's Ad Run Intake, approve the selected actions, and attach Broadcast Stopped only to the provider's Streaming Stopped trigger.

sections.title: 12. Card appearance
sections.description: Choose a readable card style for OBS, Meld, Streamlabs, or a private browser dock.

sections.title: Safety, controls, and privacy
sections.description: Use Finish Stream for the streamlined one-press path, or Suggest and Confirm for manual review. Keep all creator controls on a deck, hotkey, or operator command. Broadcast Stopped belongs only on the selected provider's stopped trigger.
sections.notice: Raid Scout stores only bounded candidate summaries, shuffle bags, stream counters, and the last 100 suggestion/raid outcomes in private local state. Twitch authentication stays inside the triggerless Streamer.bot controller and is sent only to fixed api.twitch.tv endpoints. Tokens are never relayed, logged, saved by StreamBridge, or exposed to the overlay.
